name: Binoculars two-LM perplexity-ratio screen (Qwen2.5 pair)
limitations: Measured 2026-09-16 on the seed corpus: every polished human sample scored 100 (ratio 0.71-0.84 overlapping AI ko at 0.67-0.79) — the ratio tracks register polish, not AI origin, so the member is effectively disabled (weight 0.05) pending re-anchoring on a real corpus.

Perplexity-ratio screen (Hans et al. 2024 style), not a trained detector — ratio anchors [0.85, 1.05] are provisional; measured separation on the seed corpus is weak (AI prose 0.67-0.94 vs human prose 0.77-0.82), so ensemble_weight is held at 0.25 until calibration.
Two CPU forward passes per window are expensive — max_windows bounds cost at the first 8 windows (~4k tokens).
Performer and observer must share a tokenizer family (default pair is Qwen2.5-0.5B/1.5B, ~4.3 GB total into the HF cache); point both ids at local snapshot directories to run fully offline.
Generator-agnostic in principle, but effectiveness on a specific generator must be measured, not assumed — the seed corpus currently covers Claude/Devin only.
Two forward passes per window roughly doubles the cost of the causal-lm-ppl runtime.
Prioritization signal, not a truth label.
license: Qwen2.5 is Apache-2.0; weights download to the HF cache, never committed
